_why: parse_query dispatches on the first token and returns the sub-parser's result without checking the input was consumed. A sub-parser that reads a valid PREFIX returns Ok and the remainder is silently discarded. Three independent reproducers, all this root cause: #1895's WITHIN GROUP, the bare-alias counter-example, and a statement-merge found by #1929's gate.

anchors._note: the defect: dispatch, return, no EOF check
the ONLY call site — the single insertion point for the fix
TokenType::Eof already exists; the check needs no new token

blast_radius._note: Measured across src/ tests/ examples/, not src/ alone — an src/-only count said 12 and was wrong by 33. The CODE change is one call site; the bulk of these refs are TESTS, which is the real work: every test asserting today's lenient truncation will newly fail. The brief requires enumerating and classifying that fallout, with a STOP at >15.

acceptance: parse_query errors when tokens remain after a successful sub-parse, naming the first unconsumed token and its position
a trailing semicolon, whitespace and comments are still accepted
all three reproducers are rejected by the GENERAL check, not by construct-specific guards
#1895's WITHIN GROUP guard is assessed for redundancy and REPORTED, not removed in this PR
every newly-failing test is classified: (a) was asserting truncated behaviour -> fix the test, or (b) the check is wrong -> fix the check
forbidden: weakening the check to a warning
adding a construct-specific exemption to make a test pass
removing the WITHIN GROUP guard in this PR
deleting, skipping or narrowing any test
